Selectins are a transmembrane protein family that help facilitate the rolling of leukocytes along endothelial cells during inflammation. Different selectins (P, L and S) are expressed in order to help facilitate the rolling of white blood cells in different vessels. Platelet derived selectin (on T helper cells and eosinophils) and lymph node derived selectin (on basophils) are both types of the leukocytes selectins which the name give away; however, neutrophils use L selectin. Integrins are also transmembrane proteins, but are involved in firm adhesion during the adhesion stage of migration. PECAM-1 (also known as CD31) is a transmembrane protein involved in cell to cell junction formation and is important in the transmigration of neutrophils. Fibrin is a cytoskeletal protein that is converted to fibrinogen in circulation and is essential in blood clotting. Keratin is a cytoskeletal protein which makes up structural elements of epithelial and other kits.
